body.estimand_functional: \((p,G)\longmapsto\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\), with \(\mathsf{Cov}_p\) evaluated chamberwise through \(\mathcal E_p\) and \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}\) evaluated by the terminal actual-row certificates.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node under noninjective mixing \(2\le p<q\).
sampling_model.units: Inputs are aligned population factorization data \(\mathcal R\) and the \(q+1\) population covariance matrices \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\); there is no finite-sample claim.
sampling_model.treatment: Each non-source context changes every incoming coefficient of one unknown latent target and retains every such edge. Targets are identified only up to one common latent permutation.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition applies. Baseline and intervention variances are positive and may coincide. Covariance theorems use only declared finite generic loci, including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\ne0\), cover both adjacent sign chambers, and make no pointwise claim on neutral hyperplanes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Aligned factor directions and source laws modulo common permutation and diagonal scaling are population inputs. Recovery from raw laws and finite-sample tensor estimation are outside scope.

Problem 5.2 asks whether the higher-cumulant-compatible graph class is strictly contained in the covariance-compatible graph class.
The generic-soft covariance analysis and perfect-intervention graph-recovery clause are stated for injective mixing \(p\ge q\).
The paper treats unpaired observational and interventional data under generalized faithfulness and recovers an equivalence class.

The half-trek criterion supplies a polynomial-time sufficient certificate for generic rational identifiability.

In arXiv:2410.23102v1, Theorem 3.10 transfers a semialgebraic image through an affine-birational parametrization with positive localizing denominators, and Theorem 3.11 identifies its saturated vanishing ideal.

The paper uses tree dynamic programming over the primal graph of variables co-occurring in atomic constraints to accelerate existential Fourier--Motzkin elimination and cylindrical algebraic decomposition.

body.tldr: Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit the proved terminal-copy and affine-support compatibility test. In the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), regular covariance twins are exactly a finite union of positive-real factor-line projections. For the \(p=2,q=4\) fork, all eight branches reduce losslessly to two candidate scalars and reconstruct the original five covariance equations. The mandated fixed resultant/subresultant projection attempt with all true coordinates free did not emit projection polynomials or Thom-cell certificates, so the all-chamber density gate failed. The bounded-width item is only a supporting finite-reduction result: its \(\omega_p\) premise is unused, and no compiler, complexity, or pathwidth headline is supported. The prospective LCD workflow may report corrected actual-row compatibility and verified individual covariance twins, but it cannot yet certify whether higher cumulants remove all generic covariance alternatives.

project_justification.gap: Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal asks whether covariance and higher-cumulant information distinguish compatible graph classes. After correcting Definition 3.14 to use actual intervention rows, the noninjective covariance question is the density of a union of positive-real projected branches in every full-dimensional sign-and-variance chamber. The prescribed fork-only Collins--Hong-style projection with \(s\) and \(x\) eliminated and all true coordinates left free failed before producing an explicit projection family, sign-cell refinement, or Thom samples. Thus neither the fork density alternative nor the graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criterion is established.
project_justification.niche: The proved contribution isolates the exact obstruction. Terminal compatibility has finite linkage and affine certificates, while every regular covariance twin belongs to one of at most \(2^{q-r}\) factor-line systems. The four-node fork is reduced exactly to eight bivariate systems containing every positivity, denominator, support, retention, mixing, and covariance condition. What remains is global projection geometry over all true parameters, not another collision or local Jacobian witness.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers the corrected terminal algorithm, the exact covariance-branch reduction, the complete regular two-scalar fork reduction, and a positive rational covariance collision checked in all five contexts. It proves the exact projected-union criterion and proves that the rational family together with its audited local neighborhoods cannot decide chamberwise density. The failed full-symbolic projection gate leaves the all-graph compiler as an open-ended question. No bounded-width compiler, certificate-height bound, bit complexity, pathwidth guarantee, all-graph criterion, or infinite generic-strictness family is claimed.

body.related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) derive the actual intervention-row system in Equation (20), use the observational inverse-path class in Definition 3.14, state recovery through Theorem 1.7, and pose graph and covariance questions in Problems 5.1--5.2. The terminal-copy result repairs the mismatch between the actual rows and the observational-path substitution. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) recover transitive-closure information for injective soft-intervention models; their injective result does not decide the noninjective positive-real covariance projection considered here. Half-trek, semidefinite realization, affine-birational transfer, and tree-accelerated real-elimination work remain methodological context. In particular, a standard resultant/subresultant projection over the complete true-parameter block is not the requested graph-specific criterion, and the failed fork attempt supplies no complexity comparison for a covariance-terminal-width compiler.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The mandated early-kill construction used the full twenty-four-coordinate fork support chart \(A,\Lambda^{(0)},\delta,v,t\), retained \(s\) and \(x\) as the only eliminated candidate variables, generated the eight loading-line choices from the exact covariance factors, used a Cramer chart for \(v'=v'_0+sn\), and specified a fixed coefficients--discriminants--principal-subresultants projection first in \(x\) and then in \(s\). Exact rational normalization timed out after fifty-five seconds before the first branch emitted its cleared input list. It consequently produced no explicit projection-polynomial family, no refinement of every full-dimensional true chamber, and no Thom-encoded sample points. This is a failed construction, not evidence that such certificates do not exist. Separate exact checks still verify all five covariance equalities for the rational fork family, positivity of \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\), the actual-row obstruction \(-2\), and regularity of all eight loading choices at audited points. Those local facts cannot replace the missing global classification.
body.honest_scope: All covariance-frontier claims remain in the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), on the declared theorem-specific generic loci and full-dimensional sign-and-variance chambers. Candidate twins may be variance-neutral, both signs of each true variance change are retained, and no pointwise claim is made on excluded true neutral hyperplanes. The terminal actual-row theorem is exact and independent of variance activity. The fork result is a sound-and-complete regular reduction and an exact projected-union criterion, not an all-chamber feasibility classification. The failed fixed projection attempt is recorded without rerolling to examples, local neighborhoods, or unrestricted quantifier elimination. The node presently named as a bounded-width compiler contributes only the already proved terminal and finite-branch reductions; because \(\omega_p\) is unused, it has no compiler, complexity, or pathwidth force and should be treated as a non-headline supporting proposition. The all-graph realization-or-separator compiler remains only the open-ended question. The prospective workflow may output corrected terminal compatibility and verified individual covariance twins, but not a global high-cumulant information-frontier verdict.
body.interpretation: The corrected compatible graph set is operational at population level once the aligned factor rows are available. Covariance-only alternatives are represented exactly by finite branch systems, and every returned fork candidate can be checked against each of the five original context covariance equations. The positive rational collision proves existence and local robustness, not generic covariance surplus. The single fixed all-parameter elimination attempt produced neither a dense-cover certificate nor a full-dimensional separator. Until the complete projected union is classified, the LCD consumer must report the high-cumulant-versus-covariance distinction as unresolved.
